But the problem is that the seroconversion is a process that requires the production of IgM followed by IgG. So the seroconversion is the transition from undetectable to IgM then IgG. However, the original sentence says that in 100% of infected people with positive IgG, this occurs 17-19 days after indications.

So the key is that the seroconversion (which is a process) is achieved at 17-19 days. So, the STL would need to state that the seroconversion is true (i.e., the process is complete) at that time.

But how to model that.

This is the reason that seroconversion (undetectable stage to production of IgM followed by IgG) in 100% of infected people (with positive virus-specific IgG) is achieved 17–19 days after commencement of indications [7].

What parts of the sentence make sense to translate and what parts don't? Think carefully, step-by-step through the process, and tell us about how STL could be used to capture the original semantic meaning of the natural language sentence.

Your STL response must conform to the following rules:
[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c
c : s(t_a) | "c(low)" | "c(mid)" | "c(high)" # c is the level of a species, it can be a specific value or generally just low, moderate, or high
d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days
s : IL6 | IL12 | IL1β | IL1Ra | TNFα | IL8 | IFNα | IFNβ | SARSCoV2 | IL1RN | IgM | IgG | MERSCoV | SARSCoV | CpG2216 | IL1α | CCL2 | CCR2 | IP10 | MCP1 | IFNγ | IL17 | IL27 | RANTES # Species names you can use
d_s : d_IL6 | d_IL12 | d_IL1β | d_IL1Ra | d_TNFα | d_IL8 | d_IFNα | d_IFNβ | d_SARSCoV2 | d_IL1RN | d_IgM | d_IgG | d_MERSCoV | d_SARSCoV | d_CpG2216 | d_IL1α | d_CCL2 | d_CCR2 | d_IP10 | d_MCP1 | d_IFNγ | d_IL17 | d_IL27 | d_RANTES # Names for derivatives of the species
[END RULES]

The d_s terms represent the derivative of a signal, so you may find those terms helpful for describing how signals increase or decrease. For general statements describing the levels of some species as "high" or "low" for example, you may find comparison statements helpful.

Alternatively, the sentence says that the seroconversion is achieved (i.e., the process of becoming positive) in 100% of the infected people. So, the fact that they are positive at that time.

But the translation needs to capture that the seroconversion (the process) is achieved at that time.

So, perhaps using the 'eventually' operator. For example, eventually[t_a,t_b] (some predicate).

But the exact structure is tricky. Let's think.

The original sentence: "This is the reason that seroconversion (undetectable stage to production of IgM followed by IgG) in 100% of infected people (with positive virus-specific IgG) is achieved 17–19 days after commencement of indications [7]."

Breaking it down:

- The reason is that [something] is achieved 17-19 days after indications.

This is the reason that seroconversion (undetectable stage to production of IgM followed by IgG) in 100% of infected people (with positive virus-specific IgG) is achieved 17–19 days after commencement of indications [7].

What parts of the sentence make sense to translate and what parts don't? Think carefully, step-by-step through the process, and tell us about how STL could be used to capture the original semantic meaning of the natural language sentence.

Your STL response must conform to the following rules:
[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c
c : s(t_a) | "c(low)" | "c(mid)" | "c(high)" # c is the level of a species, it can be a specific value or generally just low, moderate, or high
d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days
s : IL6 | IL12 | IL1β | IL1Ra | TNFα | IL8 | IFNα | IFNβ | SARSCoV2 | IL1RN | IgM | IgG | MERSCoV | SARSCoV | CpG2216 | IL1α | CCL2 | CCR2 | IP10 | MCP1 | IFNγ | IL17 | IL27 | RANTES # Species names you can use
d_s : d_IL6 | d_IL12 | d_IL1β | d_IL1Ra | d_TNFα | d_IL8 | d_IFNα | d_IFNβ | d_SARSCoV2 | d_IL1RN | d_IgM | d_IgG | d_MERSCoV | d_SARSCoV | d_CpG2216 | d_IL1α | d_CCL2 | d_CCR2 | d_IP10 | d_MCP1 | d_IFNγ | d_IL17 | d_IL27 | d_RANTES # Names for derivatives of the species
[END RULES]

The d_s terms represent the derivative of a signal, so you may find those terms helpful for describing how signals increase or decrease. For general statements describing the levels of some species as "high" or "low" for example, you may find comparison statements helpful.

u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is

greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c
c : s(t_a) | "c(low)" | "c(mid)" | "c(high)" # c is the level of a species, it can be a specific value or generally just low, moderate, or high
d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days

thinking prompt: Give an explanation of how you would translate the following natural language sentence into a signal temporal logic (STL) statement:
Monocyte chemotactic factor chemokine(C-C motif) ligand 2 (CCL2) was increased in the blood of infected patients as well as the transcripts of its receptor CCR2; this was associated with low counts of circulating inflammatory monocytes (Fig. 4I), suggesting a rolefor the CCL2/CCR2 axis in the monocyte chemo-attraction into the inflamed lungs.

Your STL response must conform to the following rules:
[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c
c : s(t_a) | "c(low)" | "c(mid)" | "c(high)" # c is the level of a species, it can be a specific value or generally just low, moderate, or high
d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days
s : IL6 | IL12 | IL1β | IL1Ra | TNFα | IL8 | IFNα | IFNβ | SARSCoV2 | IL1RN | IgM | IgG | MERSCoV | SARSCoV | CpG2216 | IL1α | CCL2 | CCR2 | IP10 | MCP1 | IFNγ | IL17 | IL27 | RANTES # Species names you can use
d_s : d_IL6 | d_IL12 | d_IL1β | d_IL1Ra | d_TNFα | d_IL8 | d_IFNα | d_IFNβ | d_SARSCoV2 | d_IL1RN | d_IgM | d_IgG | d_MERSCoV | d_SARSCoV | d_CpG2216 | d_IL1α | d_CCL2 | d_CCR2 | d_IP10 | d_MCP1 | d_IFNγ | d_IL17 | d_IL27 | d_RANTES # Names for derivatives of the species
[END RULES]

The d_s terms represent the derivative of a signal, so you may find those terms helpful for describing how signals increase or decrease. For general statements describing the levels of some species as "high" or "low" for example, you may find comparison statements helpful.

The STL statement would need to capture that when CCL2 and CCR2 are high (as 'is' high), then the monocyte count is low (as 'is' low). So the structure would be:

But according to the rules, the temporal operator is either 'eventually[t_a,t_b]' or 'globally[t_a,t_b]'.

[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c

d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days

So, the key elements here are:

1. **IP-10 level** – the species being measured.
2. **Significantly elevated** – indicating a statistical significance.
3. **In COVID-19 patients in week 1 of onset** – the time frame and group (mild vs severe).
4. **Compared with healthy volunteer controls** – the comparison group.
5. **P values** – the statistical significance.

Now, translating this into STL. Let's recall that STL uses temporal operators like eventually, globally, etc., and comparison operators like greater_than, less_than, is, etc.

First, the main action is that the IP-10 level was elevated in the patients. So, we need to express that the level is higher than the control group. But since it's a comparison between two groups (mild and severe), we need to account for both groups.

The sentence mentions "in week 1 of onset of symptoms in both mild and severe groups". So, the time is week 1, and the groups are mild and severe. Then, compared to healthy controls. 

In STL, we can use the 'eventually' operator to specify that this condition holds at a certain time. However, the original sentence is about a specific time point (week 1) and the comparison between groups.

[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c

	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days
s : IL6 | IL12 | IL1β | IL1Ra | TNFα | IL8 | IFNα | IFNβ | SARSCoV2 | IL1RN | IgM | IgG | MERSCoV | SARSCoV | CpG2216 | IL1α | CCL2 | CCR2 | IP10 | MCP1 | IFNγ | IL17 | IL27 | RANTES # Species names you can use

[END RULES]

Your STL response must conform to the following rules:
[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c
c : s(t_a) | "c(low)" | "c(mid)" | "c(high)" # c is the level of a species, it can be a specific value or generally just low, moderate, or high
d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days
s : IL6 | IL12 | IL1β | IL1Ra | TNFα | IL8 | IFNα | IFNβ | SARSCoV2 | IL1RN | IgM | IgG | MERSCoV | SARSCoV | CpG2216 | IL1α | CCL2 | CCR2 | IP10 | MCP1 | IFNγ | IL17 | IL27 | RANTES # Species names you can use

[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c

d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval

	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true

u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is

	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true

less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c

	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing

	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days

u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is

greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c

d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days
s : IL6 | IL12 | IL1β | IL1Ra | TNFα | IL8 | IFNα | IFNβ | SARSCoV2 | IL1RN | IgM | IgG | MERSCoV | SARSCoV | CpG2216 | IL1α | CCL2 | CCR2 | IP10 | MCP1 | IFNγ | IL17 | IL27 | RANTES # Species names you can use

What parts of the sentence make sense to translate and what parts don't? Think carefully, step-by-step through the process, and tell us about how STL could be used to capture the original semantic meaning of the natural language sentence.

Your STL response must conform to the following rules:
[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c
c : s(t_a) | "c(low)" | "c(mid)" | "c(high)" # c is the level of a species, it can be a specific value or generally just low, moderate, or high
d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days
s : IL6 | IL12 | IL1β | IL1Ra | TNFα | IL8 | IFNα | IFNβ | SARSCoV2 | IL1RN | IgM | IgG | MERSCoV | SARSCoV | CpG2216 | IL1α | CCL2 | CCR2 | IP10 | MCP1 | IFNγ | IL17 | IL27 | RANTES # Species names you can use
d_s : d_IL6 | d_IL12 | d_IL1β | d_IL1Ra | d_TNFα | d_IL8 | d_IFNα | d_IFNβ | d_SARSCoV2 | d_IL1RN | d_IgM | d_IgG | d_MERSCoV | d_SARSCoV | d_CpG2216 | d_IL1α | d_CCL2 | d_CCR2 | d_IP10 | d_MCP1 | d_IFNγ | d_IL17 | d_IL27 | d_RANTES # Names for derivatives of the species
[END RULES]

Your STL response must conform to the following rules:
[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c

d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days
s : IL6 | IL12 | IL1β | IL1Ra | TNFα | IL8 | IFNα | IFNβ | SARSCoV2 | IL1RN | IgM | IgG | MERSCoV | SARSCoV | CpG2216 | IL1α | CCL2 | CCR2 | IP10 | MCP1 | IFNγ | IL17 | IL27 | RANTES # Species names you can use

[END RULES]

greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c

d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days

[END RULES]

thinking prompt: Give an explanation of how you would translate the following natural language sentence into a signal temporal logic (STL) statement:
Most cytokines observed in previous publications of “cytokine storms” in association with disease severity (9, 10, 14) were observed only in the late stage of severe cases, mostly at 4 weeks after onset of symptom — for example, IL-6, IL-12, IL-1β, IFN-γ, IL-17, and IL-27.

What parts of the sentence make sense to translate and what parts don't? Think carefully, step-by-step through the process, and tell us about how STL could be used to capture the original semantic meaning of the natural language sentence.

Your STL response must conform to the following rules:
[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c
c : s(t_a) | "c(low)" | "c(mid)" | "c(high)" # c is the level of a species, it can be a specific value or generally just low, moderate, or high
d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days
s : IL6 | IL12 | IL1β | IL1Ra | TNFα | IL8 | IFNα | IFNβ | SARSCoV2 | IL1RN | IgM | IgG | MERSCoV | SARSCoV | CpG2216 | IL1α | CCL2 | CCR2 | IP10 | MCP1 | IFNγ | IL17 | IL27 | RANTES # Species names you can use

[END RULES]

We found that IL-6 (P<0.0001), IL-8 (P<0.0001) and TNF-α (P<0.0001) were significantly elevated in COVID-19 serum compared to healthy donor serum or plasma isolated from CAR T cell-treated patients with no CRS (Fig. 1).

What parts of the sentence make sense to translate and what parts don't? Think carefully, step-by-step through the process, and tell us about how STL could be used to capture the original semantic meaning of the natural language sentence.

Your STL response must conform to the following rules:
[BEGIN RULES]
u : less_than | greater_than | is | derivative_greater_than | derivative_less_than | derivative_is
less_than : s(t) < c # Species s is less than c
greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c
derivative_less_than : d_s(t) < d_c # The rate of change of species s is less than d_c
derivative_is : d_s(t) = d_c # The rate of change species s is close to d_c
c : s(t_a) | "c(low)" | "c(mid)" | "c(high)" # c is the level of a species, it can be a specific value or generally just low, moderate, or high
d_c : 0 # Rate of change is 0
	| "d_c(low)" # Species is slowly increasing
	| "d_c(high)" # Species is rapidly increasing
	| "-d_c(low)" # Species is slowly decreasing
	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
temporal_operator : eventually[t_a,t_b]globally(predicate) # This means that between day t_a and t_b, there is a point when the predicate becomes true for the rest of the interval
	| globally[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means the predicate is true over the entire interval from day t_a to t_b
	| eventually[t_a,t_b](phi) # This means there is at least 1 time between days t_a and t_b that the predicate is true
t_a : number | ∞ # Time in days
s : IL6 | IL12 | IL1β | IL1Ra | TNFα | IL8 | IFNα | IFNβ | SARSCoV2 | IL1RN | IgM | IgG | MERSCoV | SARSCoV | CpG2216 | IL1α | CCL2 | CCR2 | IP10 | MCP1 | IFNγ | IL17 | IL27 | RANTES # Species names you can use
d_s : d_IL6 | d_IL12 | d_IL1β | d_IL1Ra | d_TNFα | d_IL8 | d_IFNα | d_IFNβ | d_SARSCoV2 | d_IL1RN | d_IgM | d_IgG | d_MERSCoV | d_SARSCoV | d_CpG2216 | d_IL1α | d_CCL2 | d_CCR2 | d_IP10 | d_MCP1 | d_IFNγ | d_IL17 | d_IL27 | d_RANTES # Names for derivatives of the species
[END RULES]

The d_s terms represent the derivative of a signal, so you may find those terms helpful for describing how signals increase or decrease. For general statements describing the levels of some species as "high" or "low" for example, you may find comparison statements helpful.

greater_than : s(t) > c # Species s is greater than c
is : s(t) = c # Species s is close to c
derivative_greater_than : d_s(t) > d_c # The rate of change of species s is greater than d_c

	| "-d_c(high)" # Species is quickly decreasing
predicate : u | u1 and u2 | u1 implies u2 # You can combine predicates with Boolean operators
